title: Acceptance-Aware Draft Model Training for Speculative Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2609.24150v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate multiple candidate tokens that are verified by the target model in a single forward pass. Its speedup is largely determined by the acceptance length, yet existing draft-model training methods mainly optimize cross-entropy or Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence as proxies. These objectives encourage distribution matching but do not directly optimize acceptance length, and the acceptance mechanism also differs between greedy and sampling-based decoding.   In this work, we propose acceptance-length-aware training losses that directly optimize the expected number of accepted tokens within a speculative window. For greedy verification, we derive an expected accepted length (EAL) loss that explicitly maximizes expected acceptance length. translated_title: 面向投机解码的接受度感知草稿模型训练
translated_abstract: 投机解码通过使用轻量级草稿模型生成多个候选词元，并由目标模型在单次前向传播中进行验证，从而加速大语言模型（LLM）的推理。其加速效果很大程度上取决于接受长度，然而现有的草稿模型训练方法主要优化交叉熵或库尔巴克-莱布勒（KL）散度作为替代目标。这些目标函数虽然促进了分布匹配，但并未直接优化接受长度，且贪心解码与基于采样的解码之间的接受机制也存在差异。在本工作中，我们提出了接受长度感知的训练损失函数，直接优化投机窗口内被接受词元的期望数量。对于贪心验证，我们推导出期望接受长度（EAL）损失，显式地最大化期望接受长度。对于基于采样的解码，我们引入窗口总变差（WTV）损失来优化……
tldr: 该论文提出了直接优化投机窗口内期望接受词元数量的接受长度感知训练损失——针对贪心验证的期望接受长度（EAL）损失和针对采样解码的窗口总变差（WTV）损失，从而提升大语言模型推理的加速效果。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes acceptance-length-aware training losses—an Expected Accepted Length (EAL) loss for greedy verification and a Window Total Variation (WTV) loss for sampling-based decoding—that directly optimize the expected number of accepted tokens in speculative decoding to improve LLM inference speedup.
